description: Leverage the state-convergence property of the JSON parsing DFA to enable failure-free speculative parallelism. JSON's grammar has high convergence: regardless of the initial state assumed for a chunk, the DFA tends to converge to the correct state within a few bytes due to the limited number of states in the JSON state machine. Directly borrowed from Ko et al.'s speculative parallel DFA matching.
mathematical_formalization: Model JSON parsing as DFA with |Q| ~ 8-12 states. Convergence factor gamma = max_q (|reachable(q, sigma*)| / |Q|) for strings of length L. For JSON, gamma < 0.3 after L=4 bytes. Speculative speedup: S = P / (1 + (P-1) * gamma) where P = parallel units.
analogical_connections: Markov chain mixing time: rapid convergence analogous to fast-mixing chains
CPU branch prediction confidence: convergence factor serves as speculation confidence
Byzantine consensus: processors converge to same state despite different starting assumptions
implementation_hypothesis: Pre-compute the JSON DFA's convergence table for each (state, 4-byte-sequence) pair. At runtime, check first 4 bytes of each chunk boundary. If convergence guaranteed, no fixup needed; otherwise propagate correct state forward. Reduces fixup from O(chunk_size) to O(4).
experiment_seed: Build complete JSON DFA. For each 64-byte boundary in real JSON files, measure bytes needed for all starting states to converge. Plot convergence CDF. Target: >95% converge within 4 bytes.
